pack.title: “So what do you do?”
pack.description: The verdict disguised as a question. Answer it once, then ask better.

scenarios.setting: Wedding reception. A stranger asks it like a verdict, drink in hand.

replies.line: I build things. Better question — how do you know the couple?
replies.why: A short answer plus a better question takes over the conversation politely.
replies.delivery: Answer fast, ask slow. The question is the power move.

replies.why: It matches the question's energy exactly, then hands it straight back.

replies.line: I'm in sales — but weddings are my real field research. How do you know them?
replies.why: Self-deprecation plus curiosity makes you the most likable person in the circle.

replies.line: Currently? Professional cake taster. Unpaid, but I'm committed.
replies.why: An absurd job title answers the ritual while refusing the ranking.

replies.line: Loaded question for a man holding this much cake.
replies.why: It names the interrogation energy with a grin, which disarms the asker.

trap.line: I do pretty well, actually. Very well.
trap.why: Answering a status check with status accepts a game with no winners.

scenarios.setting: Networking event. Name tags, bad wine, worse questions.
scenarios.jab: What do you do? And be honest — is it actually interesting?

replies.line: It pays well. What do you do when you're not vetting people?
replies.why: It answers with unapologetic brevity, then names the vetting with a smile.
Agreeing it's boring ends the audit and the ball is in their court.

replies.line: Honestly? Some days. Tell me the interesting version of your job.
replies.why: Honesty plus an invitation turns the interrogator into the entertainment.

replies.line: I make small talk at networking events. Living the dream.
replies.why: Answering with the present moment makes you both laugh at the ritual.

scenarios.setting: Dinner party. You say you're between jobs; the table goes quiet.
scenarios.jab: Oh. So what do you… do all day?

replies.line: I interview, I read, I choose carefully. Pass the bread.
replies.why: A full dignified day plus a redirect shows the gap is a plan, not a problem.

replies.line: Whatever I want — it's temporary and I'm enjoying the plot twist.
replies.why: Framing unemployment as a chapter keeps the table curious instead of pitying.
Answering the awkwardness itself lets the whole table exhale and laugh.

trap.line: Well at least I'm not defined by my job like some people.
trap.why: Judging the table for asking turns one awkward question into a cold evening.
